title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after being falsely charged with bank theft in Fargo, North Dakota. US marshals took her from her home while she babysat a neighbor's four children. She was held nearly four months in Tennessee awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. Charges were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time. She was released on Christmas Eve and later learned she had lost her residence, car, and personal property.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck for $10m in federal court. The lawsuit says police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and her social media photo, then sought an arrest warrant without enough investigation or probable cause. It also claims the department lacked proper policies, training, and supervision for facial recognition technology. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The suit seeks accountability and more careful use of such technology.
